relations.subject: vector-search:hyperscale-reranking
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - predicate minted in vector-index-best-practices.json for this exact index-creation-time configuration dependency
relations.evidence: To enable reranking, your index must have a copy of the full vector value in addition to the quantized value. The `CREATE VECTOR INDEX` statement adds this copy of the full vector value to the index by default.

relations.subject: vector-search:reranking
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused (tradesOffAgainst) - predicate minted in vector-index-best-practices.json; same relation logged there, new evidence from this page
relations.evidence: Reranking can improve the accuracy of recall in some cases. However, it always decreases queries per second (QPS) when enabled. In many cases, you can achieve acceptable recall accuracy without reranking.

relations.subject: vector-search:persist-full-vector
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused (tradesOffAgainst) - predicate minted family-wide in vector-index-best-practices.json; not previously logged for this specific subject/object pair
relations.evidence: Storing the full vector significantly increases the size of the index. If you do not plan to use reranking, you can save space in your index by having it not save the full vector value.

relations.subject: vector-search:hyperscale-reranking
relations.note: structural link - persist_full_vector is set in the CREATE VECTOR INDEX statement's WITH clause
relations.evidence: To prevent an index from persisting the full vector, set the `persist_full_vector` attribute to `False` in the `WITH` clause of the `CREATE VECTOR INDEX` statement you use to create it
